name: Expedia Group
description: Expedia runs online travel marketplaces (Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz and others) where travelers book hotels, vacation rentals, flights and packages, and a fast-growing B2B arm that supplies the same inventory and booking technology to airlines, banks, travel agents and corporate travel companies. It mostly earns a commission-like margin on bookings it handles (about 12 percent of $119.6B of gross bookings in 2025), either as merchant (it collects the traveler's payment and pays the hotel) or as agency (the hotel pays it a commission). Advertising from hotels and brands on its sites is a smaller high-margin line. Lodging is about 80 percent of revenue; B2B grew 18 percent in 2025 while the consumer brands grew 2 percent.

sub.name: Travel booking sites and ride apps

businessLines.name: B2C (Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo and other consumer brands)
businessLines.how: Merchant model: the traveler pays Expedia, which pays the hotel later and keeps the spread. Agency model: the hotel or airline pays Expedia a commission after the stay. Plus advertising from hotels and other advertisers on the sites.
businessLines.description: Consumer travel marketplaces and advertising on them.

businessLines.how: Partners put Expedia's hotel inventory and booking engine on their own sites and pay Expedia a share of each booking; mostly merchant-model revenue that scales with partner volume.
